# Example rosters (generated by examples.py). `*` = BENIGN eater (DF never acts on its relation).

## Baseline (rules as written)

### Size bands demote LP cats/bears to "small predator": rule B makes a cougar eat beetles and slugs; an AP (grizzly man) is the web's top predator

- `TEMP_GRASS_FOREST / land / SUMMER / seed 5` seed=**GIANT_TICK**  
  roster: GIANT_TICK (giant_large_prey), BEAR_GRIZZLY_MAN (medium_pred), COUGAR (small_pred), WOMBAT (small_prey), SLUG (v_ground_fish), KOALA (small_prey), BEETLE (v_ground_fish), ELK (medium_prey), LIZARD_RHINO_TWO_LEGGED (v_ground_fish), TERMITE (v_colony)  
  edges: BEAR_GRIZZLY_MAN>COUGAR · BEAR_GRIZZLY_MAN>ELK · BEAR_GRIZZLY_MAN>GIANT_TICK · BEAR_GRIZZLY_MAN>KOALA · BEAR_GRIZZLY_MAN>WOMBAT · COUGAR>BEETLE · COUGAR>LIZARD_RHINO_TWO_LEGGED · COUGAR>SLUG · COUGAR>TERMITE

### Wolf pack: rule B + F (+1) -> wolves eat vermin and "small" prey; the 140k deer counts as small

### Singleton roster: HV seed is a 2M cm3 giant insect no flier may eat (rule E caps giant raptors at medium prey; B caps raptors at vermin)

  roster: GIANT_THRIPS (giant_large_prey)  
  edges: (none)
